input_signals.name: Clean Operating Profit Trend
input_signals.hypothesis: Improving operating profitability is more return-predictive when it is not financed by rising working capital accruals.
input_signals.reasoning: A positive operating-profit trend is more credible if it does not require firms to build receivables, inventory, or other working-capital balances. This interaction separates genuine margin or efficiency improvement from accrual-driven earnings expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( trend( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( delta( wcap, 1 ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Stable Accrual EBITDA Confirmation
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(ebitda, at), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), DELTA(lct, 1)), SUB(ADD(DELTA(dlc, 1), DELTA(txp, 1)), dp)), at), 1)), NEG(WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(ADD(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), DELTA(lct, 1)), SUB(ADD(DELTA(dlc, 1), DELTA(txp, 1)), dp)), at), 3), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent EBITDA profitability should earn stronger abnormal returns when accruals are both low and stable.
input_signals.reasoning: The profitability leg smooths EBITDA to emphasize durable operating performance rather than a one-year spike. The accrual leg combines low accrual intensity with low accrual volatility, aiming to identify firms whose profits repeatedly convert into cash rather than depending on unstable accounting adjustments.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( ebitda, at ), 3 ) ), ind_zscore( sumrank( neg( winsor( ratio( add( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), delta( lct, 1 ) ), sub( add( delta( dlc, 1 ), delta( txp, 1 ) ), dp ) ), at ), 1 ) ), neg( winsor( vol( ratio( add( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), delta( lct, 1 ) ), sub( add( delta( dlc, 1 ), delta( txp, 1 ) ), dp ) ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Margin Expansion Asset Discipline
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating margin improvement is more durable when it is not accompanied by noncash current-asset buildup.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the generic operating-profitability × Sloan-accrual product with a more specific mechanism: margin expansion is credible only if receivables, inventory, and other noncash current assets are not expanding faster than sales. Scaling by sales ties the accrual leg to the revenue base that generates the margin, avoiding redundant industry normalization and reducing exposure to a pure asset-scaled accrual anomaly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( trend( ratio( oiadp, sale ), 3 ) ), ind_zscore( neg( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), sale ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Historical Depreciation Shortfall Profit
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating profitability should underperform when depreciation charges are unusually low relative to the firm’s own history.
input_signals.reasoning: This revisits the depreciation-shortfall mechanism using a historical state rather than a noisy one-year change. High scores identify firms with strong reported operating income while depreciation and amortization charges sit near historical lows, consistent with accounting-estimate support that may later reverse.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_zscore( ts_rank( neg( ratio( dpc, at ) ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Margin Expansion Depreciation Shortfall
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating margin improvement should underperform when it coincides with unusually low depreciation charges.
input_signals.reasoning: Margin expansion can be mechanically boosted if depreciation expense is depressed by accounting estimates or asset-age effects. Conditioning the profitability trend on firm-specific depreciation shortfall targets cases where apparent operating improvement may be accounting-supported rather than cash-supported.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( trend( ratio( oiadp, sale ), 3 ) ), ind_zscore( ts_rank( neg( ratio( dpc, at ) ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Quality Anchored Margin Expansion
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 3), MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), sale), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Margin expansion should predict stronger returns when it occurs at already profitable firms and is not accompanied by noncash current-asset buildup.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier margin-discipline signal had strong cross-sectional evidence but weak portfolio alpha, possibly because margin trends alone included fragile or low-profitability improvers. This version anchors the margin trend with smoothed operating profitability and then rewards firms whose improvement is not tied up in receivables, inventory, or other noncash current assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( sumrank( trend( ratio( oiadp, sale ), 3 ), ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ) ), ind_zscore( neg( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), sale ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Historical Accrual Extreme Profit Trap
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(TS_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), DELTA(lct, 1)), SUB(ADD(DELTA(dlc, 1), DELTA(txp, 1)), dp)), at), 1), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistently profitable firms should underperform when balance-sheet accrual intensity is unusually high relative to their own history.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than using a noisy short trend in accruals, this asks whether the current accrual burden is near a firm-specific extreme. High profitability paired with historically elevated accrual intensity suggests earnings quality has deteriorated in a way that may reverse.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_zscore( ts_rank( winsor( ratio( add( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), delta( lct, 1 ) ), sub( add( delta( dlc, 1 ), delta( txp, 1 ) ), dp ) ), at ), 1 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cost Cut Working Capital Trap
input_signals.hypothesis: Apparent profitability improvement from falling SG&A intensity should underperform when noncash current assets are rising relative to sales.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the sparse tax-and-other-accrual channel with a broader, higher-coverage operating accrual mechanism. Cost cuts can temporarily lift margins, but if receivables, inventory, and other noncash current assets are simultaneously building, the improvement may reflect weak cash conversion or underinvestment rather than durable profitability.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( trend( ratio( xsga, sale ), 3 ) ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Noncash Asset Profit Productivity
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating margins are more durable when they are generated with little noncash current-asset intensity.
input_signals.reasoning: This drops the repeatedly reused depreciation-change and depreciation-trough legs entirely. The signal tests a direct operating-cycle productivity mechanism: profits are more cash-credible when each dollar of receivables, inventory, and other noncash current assets supports more operating income.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( ratio( oiadp, sale ), ratio( sub( act, che ), sale ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Supplier Stripped Cash Profit
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(oancf, apalch), invch), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating profitability should predict stronger returns when cash flow remains strong after removing supplier-financing and inventory-release effects.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the balance-sheet accrual ceiling with a cash-confirmation test that excludes two potentially temporary working-capital cash sources. The MIN structure requires both reported operating profitability and supplier-stripped cash generation, so high scores are not just generic cash-based profitability or a standalone accrual measure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( oancf, apalch ), invch ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross Profit Working Capital Productivity
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross profitability should predict stronger returns when it requires little working-capital investment relative to sales.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the repeated depreciation-trough pairing with a gross-profit operating-cycle efficiency measure. A high gross margin is more credible when it is not tied to heavy working-capital balances, indicating that the firm’s basic product economics convert into cash more efficiently.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sale ), ratio( wcap, sale ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Liability Stripped Cash Profit
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating profitability should predict stronger returns when operating cash flow remains strong after removing support from rising operating current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: Increases in non-debt operating current liabilities can temporarily inflate operating cash flow through supplier financing or accrued expenses. This signal requires reported profitability and cash generation net of that liability support, aiming to identify profits backed by customer cash rather than by stretching payables or accruals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, delta( sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ), 1 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating Margin Working Capital Turnover
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating margins should be more durable when firms generate sales with little noncash current-asset investment.
input_signals.reasoning: This fixes the ratio-cancellation issue by combining margin and noncash-current-asset turnover after separate ranking, rather than forming a raw ratio of ratios. High scores require both strong profitability per dollar of sales and efficient use of receivables, inventory, and other noncash current assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, sale ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sale, sub( act, che ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross Margin Lean Operating Cycle
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent gross margins should predict stronger returns when noncash current assets are unusually low relative to sales.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the algebraic collapse into gross profit divided by noncash current assets by requiring two distinct conditions: sustained gross profitability and a lean operating-cycle balance sheet. The firm-relative accrual leg asks whether profitability is being generated without unusually heavy receivable or inventory investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sale ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ts_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( act, che ), sale ), 1 ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistent Accrual Reliance Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), DELTA(lct, 1)), SUB(ADD(DELTA(dlc, 1), DELTA(txp, 1)), dp)), at), 1), 0), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistently profitable firms should underperform when they repeatedly report positive balance-sheet accruals.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the failed lagged-spike crossing and tests a different mechanism: recurring accrual reliance rather than a single extreme accrual event. A profitable firm that repeatedly needs positive accruals to support earnings is more likely to have profits that reverse or disappoint.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_zscore( ts_sum( indicator( winsor( ratio( add( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), delta( lct, 1 ) ), sub( add( delta( dlc, 1 ), delta( txp, 1 ) ), dp ) ), at ), 1 ), 0 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross Margin Current Asset Discipline
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 1), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent gross margins should predict stronger returns when noncash current assets are not rising relative to sales.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests whether strong product economics remain cash-efficient as the operating cycle evolves. Gross profitability is more credible when receivables, inventory, and other noncash current assets are stable or falling relative to the revenue base instead of absorbing cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sale ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( winsor( delta( ratio( sub( act, che ), sale ), 1 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: SG&A Efficiency Lean Cycle
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitability improvement from falling SG&A intensity should be more durable when the firm also runs a lean noncash working-capital cycle.
input_signals.reasoning: Cost efficiency can be genuine operating discipline or merely temporary underinvestment. Requiring high noncash-current-asset turnover helps separate scalable cost improvement from firms whose reported efficiency is paired with weak cash conversion in receivables and inventory.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( neg( trend( ratio( xsga, sale ), 3 ) ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sale, sub( act, che ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Conversion Cycle Margin
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, sale)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), sale), 1)), WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1), sale), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating margins should earn stronger returns when the cash conversion cycle is improving through lower noncash current assets and higher operating current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: The asset and liability sides of working capital have produced different cross-sectional and portfolio behavior, so this combines them into a single cash-conversion mechanism. Margins are more cash-backed when noncash current assets are not absorbing sales proceeds and operating liabilities provide normal trade-credit support.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, sale ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( neg( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), sale ), 1 ) ), winsor( ratio( delta( sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ), 1 ), sale ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Margin Turnover Deterioration Trap
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating-margin firms should underperform when noncash-current-asset turnover is deteriorating.
input_signals.reasoning: A profitable firm whose sales generated per dollar of noncash current assets is falling may be accumulating receivables, inventory, or other accrual assets behind the reported margin. This targets a reversal channel distinct from simply having a low turnover level: the deterioration itself signals weakening cash conversion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, sale ) ), ind_zscore( neg( winsor( delta( ratio( sale, sub( act, che ) ), 1 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Margin Turnover Improvement Confirmation
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating margins should predict stronger returns when noncash-current-asset turnover is improving.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a smoothed restatement of the turnover-level interaction; it tests the change in operating-cycle efficiency. High margins are more credible when the firm is generating more sales per dollar of receivables, inventory, and other noncash current assets, indicating improving cash conversion rather than a static lean balance sheet.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, sale ) ), ind_rank( winsor( delta( ratio( sale, sub( act, che ) ), 1 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross Margin Neutral Cash Confirmation
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(oancf, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), sale), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent gross profitability should predict stronger returns when cash generation remains strong after neutralizing working-capital releases and liability financing.
input_signals.reasoning: The cash leg adds back noncash current-asset investment and subtracts operating-liability increases, reducing the chance that cash flow is temporarily flattered by inventory liquidation, receivable collection, or stretched payables. The interaction asks whether strong product economics are backed by cash earnings independent of working-capital timing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sale ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( add( oancf, delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ) ), delta( sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ), 1 ) ), sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating Margin Trade Credit Coverage
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, sale)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(act, che), SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating margins should predict stronger returns when noncash current assets are well covered by operating current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the already-tested noncash-current-asset change and turnover channels by focusing on the stock balance between accrual assets and trade/accrued operating liabilities. Profits are more cash-credible when receivables, inventory, and other noncash current assets are not large relative to the operating liabilities that finance the cycle.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, sale ) ), ind_rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross Margin Net Working Capital Neutral Cash
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, DELTA(wcap, 1)), sale), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent gross margins should predict stronger returns when operating cash generation remains strong after neutralizing net working-capital timing.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the prior cash-conversion-cycle recombination with a direct cash-cover test: adding the change in working capital removes temporary cash boosts from working-capital release and restores cash suppressed by working-capital investment. The interaction asks whether durable product economics are backed by cash before working-capital timing effects.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sale ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( add( oancf, delta( wcap, 1 ) ), sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Short Term Debt Funded Profit Trap
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms should underperform when current debt is rising, suggesting reported profits are not funding the operating cycle internally.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids another working-capital-overhang variant and tests a different cash-backing failure: firms can look profitable while plugging cash needs with short-term borrowing. High scores identify firms with strong operating profitability but deteriorating near-term financing reliance, a configuration more likely to reverse or disappoint.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( dlc, 1 ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cost Discipline Neutral Cash Cover
input_signals.hypothesis: SG&A efficiency gains should predict stronger returns when they are accompanied by strong working-capital-neutral cash generation.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the already-tested SG&A trend × current-asset-discipline pair with a cash confirmation mechanism. Falling SG&A intensity is more likely to be real operating efficiency when cash flow remains strong after removing net working-capital timing effects, rather than merely reflecting accrual-supported sales or underinvestment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( neg( trend( ratio( xsga, sale ), 3 ) ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( add( oancf, delta( wcap, 1 ) ), sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt Funded Working Capital Profit Trap
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), at), 1), WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), sale), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms should underperform when noncash current-asset buildup is accompanied by rising current debt.
input_signals.reasoning: This extends the short-term-debt funding channel by requiring that debt reliance coincide with accrual investment in the operating cycle. Profits are less cash-backed when receivables, inventory, or other noncash current assets expand while the firm also borrows short term to fund liquidity needs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_zscore( sumrank( winsor( ratio( delta( dlc, 1 ), at ), 1 ), winsor( ratio( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), sale ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Repeated Current Asset Discipline Profit
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent operating profitability should be more durable when noncash current-asset intensity repeatedly declines rather than periodically expanding.
input_signals.reasoning: A single clean working-capital observation can be temporary, but repeated discipline suggests the firm consistently converts operations into cash without building accrual assets. The count-based accrual leg separates durable profitable firms from those that periodically need receivable or inventory expansion to sustain earnings.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ts_sum( indicator( neg( winsor( delta( ratio( sub( act, che ), sale ), 1 ), 1 ) ), 0 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Net Cash Retention Margin
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating margins should predict stronger returns when firms retain cash net of short-term borrowing.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from trade-credit coverage and working-capital-turnover restatements by testing whether profitable operations actually increase cash without relying on current debt. Strong margins are more credible when they translate into net cash balance growth rather than being offset by liquidity strain.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, sale ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( delta( che, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual Asset Cash Drain Profit Trap
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms should underperform when noncash current assets rise while cash balances fail to keep pace.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not another self-funded cash-flow rescaling; it focuses on balance-sheet liquidity migration from cash into receivables, inventory, and other noncash current assets. High reported profitability is less credible when the operating cycle is absorbing liquidity into accrual assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, SUB(act, che)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable gross profitability should predict stronger returns when cash balances provide a cushion against noncash current assets.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the trade-credit reciprocal with a distinct cash-cushion mechanism. A firm with a strong gross-margin floor and ample cash relative to receivables, inventory, and other noncash current assets is less likely to have profitability dependent on fragile accrual balances.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sale ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( che, sub( act, che ) ), 1 ) ) )
